data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached at different nodes along the stem in a spiral pattern, visible across multiple images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves appear grouped at the terminal end of the branch)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (leaves are single blades without leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (leaf edges are smooth, though some have physical holes/damage)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): obovate (leaf is broadest above the middle and tapers toward the base)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tip tapers to a distinct point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (base tapers to a narrow wedge shape where it meets the petiole)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single main midrib with lateral veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, forming a reticulate pattern with numerous veins extending to the margin
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): rugose (surface appears wrinkled and textured)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): present (faint hairs are visible along the midrib and leaf margins)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are very short, appearing to clasp the stem)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears rigid and brownish)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stem appears relatively smooth)
    19. Stem color: dark brown
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: The leaves are arranged in a rosette-like cluster at the tip of the branch. The leaf surface is notably textured (rugose). Some leaves exhibit physical damage in the form of holes.
